title: Homotopy-inverse criterion for fibrant categorical-pattern objects
statement:
In a fixed universe, use fully scaled categorical patterns and $P$-fibered marked objects from [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], marked products and $K^\sharp$ from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], the sharp mapping complexes and pattern model structure from [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus], and weak homotopy equivalences from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $P=(B,S,\{p_a:K_a^{\triangleleft}\to B\}_{a\in A})$ be any small such pattern, and let $f:F\to G$ be a map of $P$-fibered marked objects over $(B,S)$. Put
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(T,Z)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/(B,S)}(T\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Z).$$
The map $f$ is a weak equivalence in the pattern model structure if and only if there exist a marked map $g:G\to F$ over $(B,S)$ and marked maps
$$H:F\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to F,\qquad J:G\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to G$$
over $(B,S)$, with $H|_0=gf$, $H|_1=\operatorname{id}_F$, $J|_0=fg$ and $J|_1=\operatorname{id}_G$. Equivalently, these inverse and homotopy data exist if and only if precomposition by $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(G,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(F,Z)$ for every $P$-fibered $Z$. No finiteness assumption on the cone shapes $K_a$ is required.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Lemma B.2.4, equivalence of (1) and (2), printed p.1483; Proposition B.1.14 supplies Kan mapping complexes.

proof.text: First work in the marked model category over a point. Let $I=(\Delta^1)^\sharp$ and let $e_0:(\Delta^0)^\sharp\to I$ select vertex $0$. The unmarked vertex inclusion $\Delta^0\to\Delta^1$ is a one-dimensional horn inclusion, hence a trivial cofibration in the Kan model structure. Apply the simplicial pushout-product axiom of the marked-point model structure to this inclusion and the cofibration $\varnothing\to(\Delta^0)^\sharp$. Its pushout product is exactly $e_0$, because the simplicial tensor is $X\otimes K=X\times K^\sharp$. Thus $e_0$ is a trivial cofibration of marked simplicial sets.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4 (1) iff (2), printed p.1483, formal argument expanded using Theorem B.0.20 and Remark B.2.5; no finiteness assumption.

proof.text: For any marked pattern object $A$, put $C_A=A\times I$, with its base map obtained by projection to $A$. The initial map $\varnothing\to A$ is a cofibration, since it is injective on all simplices. The marked pushout-product assertion for the pattern model structure, applied to this initial map and $e_0$ from step 1, makes $i_0:A\to C_A$ a trivial cofibration. The projection $p:C_A\to A$ satisfies $pi_0=1_A$, so two-out-of-three makes $p$ a weak equivalence. The two endpoints give a degreewise injective map $A\amalg A\to A\times I$, hence a cofibration, and $pi_1=1_A$ also holds. These are good cylinders in exactly the sense of [lem-coef-model-cylinder-whitehead]. Every object is cofibrant, and $F,G$ are fibrant because they are $P$-fibered.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4 (1) iff (2), printed p.1483, formal argument expanded using Theorem B.0.20 and Remark B.2.5; no finiteness assumption.

proof.text: Assume $f:F\to G$ is a weak equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-model-cylinder-whitehead] inside the pattern model category, with the good cylinders $C_F=F\times I$ and $C_G=G\times I$ of step 2. The theorem gives $g:G\to F$ and maps $H:C_F\to F$, $J:C_G\to G$ whose endpoints are respectively $gf,1_F$ and $fg,1_G$. All three are morphisms of the slice category, so preserve markings and commute with the maps to $(B,S)$. These are precisely the inverse data required by the item.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4 (1) iff (2), printed p.1483, formal argument expanded using Theorem B.0.20 and Remark B.2.5; no finiteness assumption.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose the specified $g,H,J$ exist. Fix a $P$-fibered $Z$ and write $M_A=\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(A,Z)$. Precomposition gives $a=f^*:M_G\to M_F$ and $b=g^*:M_F\to M_G$. Here is the homotopy on $M_F$ explicitly. For $u:F\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Z$ and an $n$-simplex $\alpha:\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$, define $\Phi_n(u,\alpha)$ to be $u$ after the marked map $F\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to F\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ which sends $(x,s)$ in simplicial degree $m$ to $(H_m(x,\alpha\circ s),s)$. The first coordinate preserves markings because $H$ does and $\alpha$ is a map between sharply marked simplices; it preserves the base because $H$ is over $B$. The second coordinate is unchanged. For every simplex operator $\theta:[k]\to[n]$, restricting this formula replaces $(u,\alpha)$ by $(u\circ(1\times\theta),\alpha\theta)$, so it defines a simplicial map $\Phi:M_F\times\Delta^1\to M_F$. At its endpoints it is $ab=(gf)^*$ and $1_{M_F}$. Replacing $(F,H)$ by $(G,J)$ gives a simplicial homotopy $M_G\times\Delta^1\to M_G$ from $ba=(fg)^*$ to $1_{M_G}$. This is a direct calculation from the sharp mapping-complex definition and the marked-product rule.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4 (1) iff (2), printed p.1483, formal argument expanded using Theorem B.0.20 and Remark B.2.5; no finiteness assumption.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to $a:M_G\to M_F$, $b:M_F\to M_G$ and the two homotopies of step 4. It says exactly that $a$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Since $Z$ was arbitrary, the weak-equivalence testing clause of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] makes $f$ a weak equivalence. The same testing clause also identifies the last condition in the statement with being a pattern weak equivalence, completing both equivalences. The model-calculus theorem applies to every small pattern, and none of steps 1–4 restricts its cone shapes; hence no finiteness assumption on $K_a$ has entered.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4 (1) iff (2), printed p.1483, formal argument expanded using Theorem B.0.20 and Remark B.2.5; no finiteness assumption.

proof_origin.place: Lemma B.2.4 (1) iff (2), whose formal proof is expanded here with prescribed cylinders and explicit mapping-complex homotopies. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q96-007e598bf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item (5 steps, no new nodes) and every cited statement in full: def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy, lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus, lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model, lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper, lem-coef-model-cylinder-whitehead and lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak. I also read the Whitehead leaf's Mathlib match in Homotopy.lean (whitehead and leftHomotopy).

Step 1: {0}⊂Δ^1 is the horn Λ^1_0, so it is a Kan trivial cofibration. Its pushout product with ∅→(Δ^0)^♯, using the tensor X×K^♯, is exactly e_0.

Step 2: the pattern pushout-product clause applied to ∅→A and e_0 gives i_0 as a trivial cofibration. Two-out-of-three then makes p a weak equivalence. (i_0,i_1) is injective on simplices, so it is a cofibration. This meets the good-cylinder definition clause by clause. Every object is cofibrant, and fibrant is the same as P-fibered.

Step 3: the endpoint orders match the item (H|0=gf, H|1=id; J|0=fg, J|1=id).

Step 4: I checked Φ by hand. It is simplicial, it preserves markings and is over B, it is natural in θ, and its endpoints are ab=(gf)^* and the identity. The same holds for J.

Step 5: the tool lemma applies with u=f^*, v=g^*, either endpoint order allowed. The model-calculus testing clause then gives both equivalences.

The statement is unchanged and matches its only citer, lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison. There is no cycle and no duplicate in the DAG. Edge cases (∅ objects, empty pattern family and empty K_a, no basepoints) are fine. I accept the declared tool_use of lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak: its unit sk-prop-sf-cbc is outside the item's route, it is a generic black box applied after the homotopies are built, and it replaces no unit step. HA B.2.4 is not archived, so the source match is from my own knowledge of that lemma. The proof stands on the cited statements, and proof_origin=agent with WANTED is correct. No SGA is used and no fixes were needed.

lean.statement: theorem fibrant_pattern_homotopy_inverse {P : CategoricalPattern.{u}} {F G : Object P} (f : F ⟶ G) (hF : IsCategoricalPatternFibered P F) (hG : IsCategoricalPatternFibered P G) : (weak f ↔ ∃ (g : G ⟶ F) (H : (tensor (SSet.Marked.sharp (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}))).obj F ⟶ F) (J : (tensor (SSet.Marked.sharp (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}))).obj G ⟶ G), SSet.ι₀ ≫ H.map = (f ≫ g).map ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ H.map = 𝟙 F.underlying.underlying ∧ SSet.ι₀ ≫ J.map = (g ≫ f).map ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ J.map = 𝟙 G.underlying.underlying) ∧ ((∃ (g : G ⟶ F) (H : (tensor (SSet.Marked.sharp (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}))).obj F ⟶ F) (J : (tensor (SSet.Marked.sharp (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}))).obj G ⟶ G), SSet.ι₀ ≫ H.map = (f ≫ g).map ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ H.map = 𝟙 F.underlying.underlying ∧ SSet.ι₀ ≫ J.map = (g ≫ f).map ∧ SSet.ι₁ ≫ J.map = 𝟙 G.underlying.underlying) ↔ ∀ Z : Object P, IsCategoricalPatternFibered P Z → IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (mapSharpPre f Z))
